captions: 7:40 a.m. The new passport lies next to the old one.
Old photo: 20, braces, big plans. New photo: 30.
Mum looks over your shoulder: “Where did ten years go?”
At 20, in an exam hall, you made a promise.
“After my degree, I'll get serious with Allah.”
Then the job. Then the flat. Then ten years.
The clock on the wall never waited. Not once.
You don't wait for 40. You roll out your mat.
Two rak'ahs of Duha. Sunlight on your hands.
The next ten years start here. With Him.

post.caption:
Two passport photos. 10 years apart. How many for Allah? 🤍

We always say “after”: after the degree, after the job, after the flat. And the years don't wait.

“So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it.” (99:7)

This morning: two rak'ahs of Duha. Before the day runs off.
